bug_semantics: free5GC NEF treats an outbound PFD-subscription notification failure as process-fatal. PfdChangeNotifier.FlushNotifications() asynchronously POSTs a PfdChangeNotification to the stored subscriber notifyUri; on any client error (connection refused, DNS failure, TLS error, timeout) it calls logger.PFDManageLog.Fatal(err). PFDManageLog is a logrus.Entry, so Fatal is os.Exit(1)-equivalent: it bypasses Gin recovery, deferred cleanup, and connection draining and terminates the entire NEF process. An attacker who can create a PFD subscription with an unreachable notifyUri and then trigger a PFD change (AF traffic-influence + PFD subscription + PFD transaction) gets a deterministic NEF crash. The PFD transaction itself returns 201; the exit happens on the async notify. In v4.2.1 the trigger chain is unauthenticated because the NEF SBI route groups lack inbound auth (tracked separately in free5gc#858/#859/#862); this case is the Fatal-on-delivery-failure defect (CWE-617/CWE-755/CWE-20).
flaw_origin: The fatal-on-notify-error mechanism was first written in free5gc/nef commit a39681cbb8e982ede4e7f36eef7b09f38c0df3db (feat(nef): Implement notification mechanism, author/committer briasp8210 <briantaipei8210@gmail.com>, 2021-01-25 / 2021-03-05). That commit added PfdNotifyContext.flushNotifications() in internal/processor/pfd_handler.go, spawning a goroutine that calls NotificationApi.NotificationPost to the subscriber URI and, on err != nil, logger.PFDManageLog.Fatal(err), plus the leftover TODO 'Handle the response of notification properly'. Immediate parent 3d054a1804771d9c6296368093c0f04941b1e62f has no PfdNotifyContext, no NotificationPost, and no PFDManageLog.Fatal.
